name: Crypto investor attention from Google search volume

origin.source_title: Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency (NBER w24877; Review of Financial Studies 2021)

how_it_works.simple: When lots of people suddenly search for 'Bitcoin' on Google, the price has tended to rise over the next couple of weeks.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a restaurant that gets busier the week after it trends on social media.
how_it_works.precise: Construct weekly Google search volume for the coin name (de-trended) and sort weeks into quintiles. Liu and Tsyvinski find a one standard deviation rise in Bitcoin search predicts a 2.3 percent higher 2-week-ahead return.

rule: Each Sunday, compute the change in Google Trends search index for 'Bitcoin' versus its trailing average; hold BTC next week if the change is in the top quintile of past values (cutoffs from past data only), otherwise hold cash.
economic_rationale: Attention brings new retail buyers whose demand pushes prices up with a lag, consistent with Da, Engelberg and Gao style attention effects cited by Liu and Tsyvinski.
why_it_might_fail: Google Trends values are rescaled each download and revised, which can create silent lookahead. Attention spikes also come before crashes. The evidence comes from 2011-2018, mostly one bubble.

reported_results.source: Liu and Tsyvinski NBER w24877, introduction and Section 4
reported_results.notes: Weekly Sharpe of the top attention quintile (11.20 percent mean weekly return) vs 1.07 percent and Sharpe 0.08 for the bottom quintile. Quintile cutoffs are full sample in this table; the paper reports an out-of-sample cutoff version also positive.

implementations.notes: Unofficial Google Trends client; repository is archived per the GitHub API.

relevance.reason: A free attention signal that could be tried on currency names or macro terms, though evidence is crypto-only and short.
